stories.summary: Export opt-in OpenTelemetry traces for dashboard requests and story dispatch
stories.description: Observability gap: no tracing. Add an opt-in OTLP exporter; off by default; correlation id carried as a span attribute.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-28 on master cd09a83 - a stand-in of OT-01 and OT-02 together (pipeline/telemetry.py no-op hooks; a span call after `call_next` in app/dashboard.py `_enforce_api_key`; a lifecycle sink subscribed in `build_bus()` only when PIPELINE_OTEL_ENDPOINT is set; an authz counter call in `authorize()`; a gauge call in `scan_all_plans`; two pinned requirements.txt lines): 17748 passed / 21 skipped, 0 conflicts. The OpenTelemetry packages were not installed for the run, so the enabled path is graded only by this story's own tests. Four other failures are environment-only and fail identically on untouched master in the planning container (test_aider_harness_availability x2: proxy-injected GH_TOKEN; test_docs_have_no_personal_home_path: the container HOME is the root user's home, which the guard bans by value; test_remote_sync ssh: no ssh binary).

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

WHAT TO BUILD (new module pipeline/telemetry.py):
1. `PIPELINE_OTEL_ENDPOINT` unset = no-op (no OTel import cost: import lazily); set = OTLP/HTTP exporter with `service.name=fagan-pipeline`. Add `opentelemetry-sdk` and `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http` to requirements.txt pinned to exact versions (code-review.md: pin anything a gate depends on).
2. Spans: one per dashboard `/api/` request (a few lines in the existing app/dashboard.py middleware: method, route template, status, correlation_id - never query strings, bodies or headers). Pipeline lifecycle (dispatch, review, merge, park) is traced from the event bus, not by editing pipeline/dispatch.py (987 lines) or pipeline/merge.py: register a telemetry sink in pipeline/event_wiring.py `build_bus()` that turns each lifecycle event into a span carrying plan, story key, event type, outcome and backend/provider name - never prompts, briefs or model output.
3. Exporter errors never break a request or a tick (log WARNING with the error type once per minute).

TESTS: no-op when unset (and opentelemetry not imported); with an in-memory exporter, a request yields one span with the allowed attributes only; a published dispatch event yields a span with its outcome; a raising exporter does not fail the request.

GENERAL RULES (every step of this story):
- Write the failing tests first (CLAUDE.md Step 3) and confirm they fail on an assertion, not an import error.
- Verify with the full suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` AND `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .` AND `.venv/bin/python scripts/check_line_limit.py`; all must be green before you finish. Report pass/fail counts in the PR description.
- A new test file that imports any `pipeline.*` module must `import pipeline.server` first (pre-existing import cycle). Copy the idiom in tests/unit/test_triage_cap_silent_skip.py.
- Bind a non-operator principal in tests the way tests/unit/test_patch_plan_enforcement.py does (`pipeline.actor.bind_principal`); never add an `actor` parameter to any MCP tool (a guard test forbids it).
- The harness scratchpad `.agent_scratchpad.md` stays untracked. Commit only the files this brief names plus the new test files it asks for. Add no helper scripts, dumps or module copies.
- Never modify an existing test except as this brief pre-authorizes, with the literal edit given. If another pre-existing test fails because of a change this brief requires, do NOT undo the required change - stop and report the conflict, naming the test and the requirement it contradicts.
- Comments and docs you write must stay true after later stories merge: state the invariant, never "until story X lands".
- Cumulative artifacts (the REFERENCE.md policy table, the IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md section 4 rows, `REMOTE_*` sets): assert only what YOU add or remove (membership/absence), never the full contents, an exact count, or a hash.
- Error messages and logs name the action and the principal subject only - never a token, secret, payload, path or exception text (Secure-by-Design).
- Commit message: Conventional Commits (`<type>(<scope>): <subject>`, subject <=72 chars), body explains why; put the story key in the body. If you change an existing test as pre-authorized, the body must say which test and why (CLAUDE.md Step 4).

stories.summary: Document the OpenTelemetry endpoint and metric names in REFERENCE.md
stories.description: Docs follow-up to OT-01/OT-02: neither story documented the opt-in switch or the metric surface.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: docs-only change - REFERENCE.md only, no production code. The impact is limited to the two docs guards: tests/unit/test_readme_reference_split.py byte-compares the `## MCP tools reference` section (do not touch that section) and tests/unit/test_docs_have_no_personal_home_path.py rejects a home path in docs (use `~` or a placeholder).

[no-new-tests] Documentation only; the existing docs guards cover the change. Do not write a new test suite.

WHAT TO DOCUMENT in REFERENCE.md, in the Configuration section next to the other `PIPELINE_*` tables (read pipeline/telemetry.py on master for the exact names and defaults - do not invent any):
1. `PIPELINE_OTEL_ENDPOINT` - unset (the default) means no OpenTelemetry import and no export; set means an OTLP/HTTP exporter with service name `fagan-pipeline`. Say that exporter failures never fail a request or a tick, and that a warning is logged at most once a minute.
2. A short subsection listing the metric names with what each measures and its labels: `pipeline.dispatch.outcomes{outcome}`, `pipeline.authz.decisions{action,outcome}` (enumerated `Action` values; never a principal - it is PII and unbounded), `pipeline.merge.results{result}`, and the gauges `pipeline.stories{status}` and `pipeline.capacity.in_use`, both read from the manifest snapshot the scheduler tick publishes (a failed tick keeps the previous snapshot).
3. One sentence that every label value is validated against an enum before the meter is touched, so a new series cannot be minted by an unexpected value.

Do not document spans here - they belong to OT-01's own text if it added any; read the file first and extend what exists rather than duplicating it.

GENERAL RULES: verify with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_readme_reference_split.py tests/unit/test_docs_have_no_personal_home_path.py` AND `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .` AND `.venv/bin/python scripts/check_line_limit.py`; commit as `docs(telemetry): <subject>` with the story key in the body. Change only REFERENCE.md.
